title: Finite-stratum detection of strict completion and cohomological vanishing
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_F$ with its induced $\ell$-adic norm topology, and a uniformizer $\pi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$, put $B_T=p_T^*\underline A$ and $k_{n,T}=(A/\pi^n)_T$ for $n\ge1$. Use the small pro-étale sites and universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and the ordinary unbounded derived module categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Write $C_T(K)=R\varprojlim_{n\ge1}\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes^L_{B_T}k_{n,T})$ and $c_{T,K}:K\to C_T(K)$ for the specified strict-tower completion unit [sk-def-pe-derived-completion, lem-pe-completion-triangle-comparison].
Let $W$ be qcqs, with a finite partition by constructible locally closed subschemes $s_\alpha:S_\alpha\hookrightarrow W$ [def-constructible-stratification]. Choose a pro-étale cover $\{U_{\alpha i}\to S_\alpha\}_i$ for each stratum. For $K\in D(B_W)$ write $K_{\alpha i}$ for its iterated inverse image on $U_{\alpha i}$. Then $c_{W,K}$ is an isomorphism if and only if every $c_{U_{\alpha i},K_{\alpha i}}$ is an isomorphism. For every integer $q$, $H^q(K)=0$ if and only if every $H^q(K_{\alpha i})=0$.
These assertions can be tested on a finite rooted binary tree of qcqs locally closed subschemes with root $W$, each internal vertex split into a quasi-compact open subscheme and its closed complement. The nonempty leaves partition $W$; each leaf $L$ has an actual morphism $t_L:L\to S_{\alpha(L)}$ whose composite with $s_{\alpha(L)}$ is its branch morphism to $W$. The base changes $U_{\alpha(L)i}\times_{S_{\alpha(L)}}L$ form covering families of the leaves. If a $B_W$-module $M$ has scalar models $M|_{U_{\alpha i}}\simeq B_{U_{\alpha i}}\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{P_{\alpha i}}$, with finitely presented $A$-modules $P_{\alpha i}$, its restrictions on these leaf covers have the same scalar modules and the same finite scalar presentation matrices. Empty leaves contribute the zero module category. Thus these leaf-cover restrictions detect both the vanishing of the cone of the specified completion unit and cohomological vanishing of any given complex. No ordering of the original strata with a globally open stratum, Noetherianity, or invertibility of $\ell$ is assumed.

proof.text: Exact pullback commutes with each homology functor. Apply the preceding module criteria to H^q(K), keeping q arbitrary. Pullback composition identifies the leaf-cover branch restrictions, and the identity comparison returns the tree root to K. This proves both degreewise detection assertions and, by homology detection in the derived category, zero-detection for arbitrary unbounded objects.

proof.text: Use the existing strict_completion_restriction_comparison. Its IsIntegral clause identifies its unit with the specified strict Roos augmentation on every K-flat representative; its Comparison.unit clause identifies the pulled unit for each immersion, weakly etale morphism and their composites. Choose a flat K-flat representative P of K. The distinguished mapping-cone triangle shows completeness of each restriction is equivalent to vanishing of the corresponding restriction of completionCone P. Apply the zero-detection from the preceding step to that cone, both on original strata covers and on the recursive leaf covers. This uses the unit equation, not just finite quotient comparisons.

proof.text: For each supplied scalar presentation, the existing scalar free and matrix comparisons identify extension of its scalar cokernel with the cokernel of the same scalarMatrix. Realize the latter as inverse image from the point of the condensed cokernel of the same entries. The adopted point pullback comparison preserves this condensed cokernel. Choose a finite presentation only to prove existence of the scalar-model pullback isomorphism; for every separately supplied matrix use the same entries, ranks and cokernel comparisons. Compose with the pullback-square equality and module pullback composition. Rank-zero presentations use the same biproduct and cokernel formulas.

It does not require exchanging arbitrary inverse image with completion or any extra boundedness hypothesis.
